plan-goryokaku.hook: A perfect five-point star of snow, seen from 90 m above.
moments: Ride the fast lift up Goryokaku Tower to the deck at about 90 m.
Look straight down at the white star shape and the frozen moat around it.
Stand on the glass floor panel and look at the ground far below your feet.
Walk into the fort and see the Hakodate Magistrate's Office, a wooden building rebuilt in 2010.
Find the statue of Hijikata Toshizo, the Shinsengumi leader who died in this war in 1869.
plan-goryokaku.tip: Go up near sunset. In winter the 'Hoshi no Yume' lights outline the star after dark, so you see it by day and night.

plan-onuma.hook: Catch small fish through a hole in a frozen lake, then eat them fried.
moments: Walk onto the frozen lake with volcano Komagatake standing white behind the small islands.
Sit in a fishing tent over a hole in the ice and pull up tiny wakasagi smelt.
Eat your catch as hot, crispy tempura right after fishing.
Ride a snowmobile across the snowy lake if you want speed.
Buy a box of Onuma dango at Numanoya, made since 1905: soy and red bean, or soy and sesame.
plan-onuma.tip: The dango box is shaped like the two lakes, with the dango as the islands. Eat it the same day; it goes hard.

plan-niseko.hook: Deep, dry powder snow with Mt Yotei standing in front of every run.
moments: Take the first lift and ski fresh powder while the snow is still soft and untouched.
Stop on the slope and look across the valley at Mt Yotei, a perfect white cone.
Ski the Hanazono tree runs through birch forest (good skier) on the all-mountain pass.
Practice turns on the gentle slopes by the Ace Family lift in an English group lesson (beginner).
Ski under the lights at night, with snow falling through the lamp beams.
plan-niseko.tip: Powder is best in the first two hours. Eat dinner in Kutchan town; it costs much less than Hirafu village.

plan-otaru-canal.hook: Stone warehouses, gas lamps and snow: an old harbor town at dusk.
moments: Stand on Asakusa Bridge for the classic view down the canal with the warehouses on the left.
Walk the stone path by the water as the gas lamps turn on one by one.
Watch the snow on the warehouse roofs turn blue, then orange in the lamp light.
Warm up with a local beer inside Otaru Soko No.1, a brewery in an old canal warehouse.
plan-otaru-canal.tip: Arrive at about 16:00, before the lamps come on at about 16:30. You get the blue sky and the lights in one visit.

plan-sakaimachi.hook: A snowy street of glass lamps, music boxes and a whistling steam clock.
moments: Walk into Kitaichi Hall, a dark old warehouse lit only by 167 oil lamps.
Look through the Kitaichi Glass shops for hand-made glass cups and small lamps.
Eat LeTAO's Double Fromage cheesecake, soft and cold, at the main shop.
Stand at the steam clock outside the Music Box Museum and hear it whistle a tune every 15 minutes.
Listen inside the music box museum, where thousands of small boxes play at once.
plan-sakaimachi.tip: Be at the steam clock on the hour; it also lets out a big cloud of steam then. Walk slowly, the street is icy.

plan-otaru-sushi.hook: Winter fish from the port, cut in front of you at the counter.
moments: Walk up Sushi-ya Dori and choose from about 20 small sushi shops.
Sit at the counter and watch the chef slice fish from the Otaru port.
Eat a lunch set of nigiri with sea urchin, salmon roe and local white fish.
Finish with a hot bowl of miso soup while snow falls outside.
plan-otaru-sushi.tip: Go at lunch; the same sets cost much less than at dinner. Ask the chef for 'jizakana', the local fish of the day.

plan-ramen-mura.hook: Eight Asahikawa ramen shops in one building, hot bowls in deep cold.
moments: Walk the row of eight shops and pick the two that look best to you.
Order a mini bowl of shoyu ramen with pork and seafood soup.
See the thin layer of lard on top that keeps the soup hot to the last sip.
Taste the firm, wavy Asahikawa noodles, then walk to the next shop for bowl two.
plan-ramen-mura.tip: Order the mini size (ミニ) at each shop. Some shops close early now, so arrive before 19:00.

plan-asahiyama.hook: King penguins walk past you through the snow, close enough to touch.
moments: Stand in the front row by 10:40 and wait for the penguins to come out.
Watch the king penguins walk in a line through the snow, only one step from you.
Walk through the glass tunnel under the penguin pool and watch them fly through the water.
Put your head up into the small glass dome in the polar bear area and see a bear look at you.
Watch seals swim up and down the tall glass tube in the seal house.
plan-asahiyama.tip: Stand on the route by 10:40. The walk is at 11:00 and 14:30; it can stop if the weather is bad.

plan-blue-pond.hook: A frozen pond with dead trees, lit in changing colors at night.
moments: Walk about five minutes on packed snow from the car park, in the dark and quiet.
See the snow-covered pond and the tall dead larch trees standing in it.
Watch the lights change the trees and snow from blue to purple to green.
Feel the cold at about -15°C, and hear only the crunch of snow under your boots.
plan-blue-pond.tip: Wear boots with grip and your warmest layers. Stand at the end of the path for a clear view of the tree line.

plan-shirahige.hook: Water pours out of a cliff into a river that is bright blue.
moments: Walk onto Shirogane Bridge, called the Blue River Bridge, in Shirogane Onsen.
Look down at the 30 m falls pouring out of the rock face, not from a river above.
See the blue water between white snow and ice on the rocks.
Stay as the lights come on and the blue river glows at dusk.
plan-shirahige.tip: Come at dusk, before the Blue Pond. You see the blue color in the last daylight, then the night lights.

plan-beer-museum.hook: Drink a beer made to an 1877 recipe in a red-brick building from 1890.
moments: Walk up to the red-brick building with the red star on top, the old Kaitakushi symbol.
Follow the Premium Tour guide through the history of Japan's oldest beer brand.
Taste two beers in the Premium Lounge: Black Label and the reproduced 'Sapporo Seibakushu'.
Walk next door to the Beer Garden and grill all-you-can-eat Jingisukan lamb with beer.
plan-beer-museum.tip: Book the Premium Tour online. It is for people 20 and over only and takes about 70 minutes. Closed on Mondays.

plan-daruma.hook: Sapporo's lamb grill since 1954: smoke, fat and a tiny counter.
moments: Wait in the queue outside in the snow, then squeeze onto a stool at the counter.
Watch the staff put a piece of fat on top of the hot dome-shaped iron pan.
Grill lamb on the dome while onions and leeks cook in the juices at the edge.
Dip the lamb in the sweet soy sauce and eat it with rice and kimchi.
Ask for hot tea in your leftover sauce at the end and drink it like soup.
plan-daruma.tip: The queue is shorter after 22:00. Wear clothes you do not mind; they will smell of lamb smoke.

plan-nijo.hook: A seafood breakfast bowl heavy with crab, sea urchin and salmon roe.
moments: Walk the market street past boiled hairy crabs and king crab legs on ice.
Sit in a small shop and order a rice bowl with uni, crab and ikura.
Pop the orange salmon roe on your tongue and taste the sweet uni.
Try grilled scallops or crab from a stall on the street.
plan-nijo.tip: Go early, before 09:00. Shops are quieter and the seafood is fresh. Check the price of each bowl before you order.

plan-garaku.hook: Sapporo's own curry: a thin spicy soup full of big pieces of meat.
moments: Take a number from the machine at the door and walk around until your turn.
Choose your spice level and your soup, based on Japanese dashi stock.
Eat the soft chicken leg or the grilled pork kakuni with big grilled vegetables.
Dip spoonfuls of rice into the hot soup and feel the spice warm you up.
plan-garaku.tip: Start with a low spice level. The number system lets you shop nearby instead of standing in the cold.

plan-odori.hook: Watch giant snow sculptures being built for the Snow Festival.
moments: Go up Sapporo TV Tower to the deck at about 90 m, above the east end of Odori Park.
Look down along the long white park toward the mountains in the west.
Walk the park blocks and watch trucks, cranes and teams shape huge blocks of snow.
See wooden frames and scaffolding around sculptures the size of buildings.
plan-odori.tip: Go up the TV Tower first for the full view, then walk the park west. Do not enter the fenced work areas.

plan-moiwa.hook: All of Sapporo lit below you from a 531 m mountain top.
moments: Ride the ropeway up the snowy mountain, then the small cable car to the summit.
Watch the sunset at about 16:45 as the sky turns orange over the city.
Stay as the city lights come on and fill the whole plain below.
Ring the bell at the top of the deck, a favorite spot for couples.
Warm up with a drink in The Jewels restaurant, next to the big windows.
plan-moiwa.tip: Arrive by 16:15 to see sunset and the night view. Buy the priority ticket in the evening to skip the queue.

plan-turnpike.hook: Fourteen km of smooth, wide curves climbing from the sea to 1,000 m.
moments: Pay the toll at the Odawara gate and start the long climb into the mountains.
Drive the flowing curves through cedar forest, with Sagami Bay opening up behind you.
Feel the air get colder and see snow on the roadside as you climb.
Park at the top at Taikanzan and look at the sports cars in the car park.
plan-turnpike.tip: Check @turn819 on X the same morning for ice and tyre rules. Drive it late morning, after the ice melts.

plan-taikanzan.hook: Mt Fuji rises white behind Lake Ashi, right from the car park.
moments: Step out of the car into air a few degrees below zero.
Stand at the rail and see Mt Fuji above Lake Ashi and the Hakone mountains.
Walk the car park and look at the sports cars that stop here on weekends.
Warm up with a hot drink in the rest area café.
plan-taikanzan.tip: Come before noon. The winter air is clearest in the morning, and clouds often cover Fuji after lunch.

plan-fun2drive.hook: You drive a real JDM car on Hakone mountain roads, a guide car in front.
moments: Pick your car in Sengokuhara: GT-R, Supra, RX-7 or Silvia.
Adjust the seat, feel the manual gear stick, and follow the guide car out.
Drive the Hakone mountain curves while the engine sound fills the cabin.
Stop with the guide and take photos of your car with the snowy mountains behind it.
plan-fun2drive.tip: Book 1 to 2 months ahead, ask for a manual car, and get the no-minimum-licence-years rule confirmed in writing.

plan-otome.hook: Mt Fuji fills the view as you drive down from Hakone to Gotemba.
moments: Pull in at the Otome Pass rest stop at the top of the pass.
Look out at Mt Fuji, big and white above the Gotemba plain.
Drive down slowly in low gear through the shaded, icy curves.
plan-otome.tip: Use low gear and do not brake hard. Shaded corners on the way down stay icy all day.

plan-oshino.hook: Water so clear you see five metres to the bottom of the pond.
moments: Walk the village lanes past thatched-roof houses with Mt Fuji above them.
Stand at Wakuike, the deepest pond, and look into the blue water and small cave.
See the water steam a little in the cold air. The springs stay about 11 to 14 °C.
Eat grilled mochi and a hot bowl of soba from the stalls.
plan-oshino.tip: Go before 10:00, before the tour buses. The paid Hannoki museum pond is not one of the real eight springs.

plan-chureito.hook: The red pagoda, Mt Fuji and the sunrise: the most famous photo of Japan.
moments: Climb the 398 stone steps in the dark with a phone light, breath steaming.
Find a spot on the viewing deck by 06:30, in the freezing morning air.
Watch the first sun turn the top of Mt Fuji pink behind the five-storey pagoda.
See the town of Fujiyoshida wake up below the hill.
plan-chureito.tip: Be on the deck by 06:30 for sunrise at 06:47. Wear shoes with grip; the steps can be icy.

plan-lake-kawaguchi.hook: Mt Fuji straight across the lake, turning orange at sunset.
moments: Park at Oishi Park on the quiet north shore of Lake Kawaguchi.
Walk to the water's edge and see Mt Fuji across the lake.
Watch the snow cap turn orange and then pink as the sun goes down.
Look for Fuji's reflection on the water if the wind is calm.
plan-lake-kawaguchi.tip: Arrive by 16:30 for sunset at about 16:55. The reflection is best when the lake has no wind.

plan-zao-onsen.hook: Milky, very acidic sulfur water in a snowy mountain village.
moments: Walk the steep village streets in the snow and smell the sulfur in the air.
Soak in a small old public bath like Kawarayu, Kamiyu or Shimoyu for a few hundred yen.
Feel the strong acid water (about pH 1.6) sting a little on the skin.
Eat Genghis Khan grilled lamb or Yamagata tama-konnyaku to warm up.
plan-zao-onsen.tip: Take off silver jewellery before the bath. Soak for short times; the acid water is strong.

plan-zao-ski.hook: Ski 10 km from the snow monsters at the top down to the village.
moments: Ride the ropeway up and see the frozen trees all around you.
Ski the long Juhyo course between snow monsters, about 10 km to the bottom.
Learn on the gentle, wide Uenodai slope right next to the village.
Stop for a hot lunch in a slope-side restaurant with snow on the windows.
plan-zao-ski.tip: Book an English private lesson for the beginner before the trip. Bring your own boots if over 28 cm.

plan-zao-juhyo.hook: Frozen trees shaped like giant white monsters, lit in colour at night.
moments: Ride the Zao Ropeway up through the dark forest to Jizo Sancho station at 1,661 m.
Step out into −10 °C and hear the snow crunch under your boots.
Walk among the snow monsters, lit in blue, green and purple.
Find the stone Jizo statue at the top, almost buried in snow.
Ride back down and go straight into a hot sulfur bath.
plan-zao-juhyo.tip: Light-up dates for 2027 come out in December. Last ropeway up is about 19:50. Cover your face; the wind is very cold.

plan-ryokan-zao.hook: Sulfur baths, kaiseki dinner and a yukata, next to the ropeway.
moments: Leave your bags, change into the yukata and go straight to the milky sulfur bath.
Eat a many-course kaiseki dinner in your yukata.
Walk to the other Takamiya inns in the village and try their baths for free.
Soak again late at night while snow falls outside.
plan-ryokan-zao.tip: If you go to the snow monster light-up, ask for the late dinner time. Ask for a private bath if you have tattoos.

plan-sendai-st.hook: Thick charcoal-grilled beef tongue, six shops in one row inside the station.
moments: Walk the 3rd floor Gyutan Street and pick a shop: Rikyu, Date no Gyutan or Kisuke.
Order the teishoku set, thick cut, with barley rice and oxtail soup.
Bite into the chewy, smoky tongue with a little green chili miso.
Buy a gyutan ekiben for the Hayabusa north. Pull the string and the box heats itself.
plan-sendai-st.tip: Ask for 厚切り (atsugiri, thick cut). Go before 18:00 or after 20:00 to skip the longest lines.

plan-matsushima.hook: About 260 small pine islands, and hot grilled oysters by the sea.
moments: Ride the Senseki Line 40 minutes from Sendai to Matsushima-Kaigan.
Cross the short bridges to Godaido, the small temple hall on its own rock.
Walk the long red Fukuura bridge to the island and look back at the bay.
Eat grilled oysters, hot and salty, in winter oyster season.
plan-matsushima.tip: Optional stop. Take the 50-minute island boat only if you have time; the bridges give good views for free.

plan-kanemori.hook: Red brick harbour warehouses from 1887, snow on the roofs at dusk.
moments: Walk along the small canal between the red brick warehouses as the lights come on.
Look in the shops of BAY Hakodate and Kanemori Yobutsukan.
Eat dinner and drink local beer in the Hakodate Beer Hall.
Walk the snowy harbour front with the bay dark beside you.
plan-kanemori.tip: Come at dusk, right after the lights come on, for the best photos of the snowy bricks.

plan-mt-hakodate.hook: City lights on a narrow strip of land between two black bays.
moments: Ride the big ropeway gondola up 334 m in a few minutes.
Stand on the top deck and watch the sun go down over the sea.
See the city lights come on, making the famous shape between the two bays.
Warm your hands in the indoor observation room after the cold wind.
plan-mt-hakodate.tip: Go up about 16:15 for sunset at 16:36. The road is closed to cars in winter, so take the ropeway.

plan-asaichi.hook: Catch a live squid yourself and eat it seconds later, still moving.
moments: Walk the morning market stalls past piles of crab, uni and ikura.
Catch a live squid with a rod at the Ekini Market squid pool.
Watch staff slice it on the spot. Eat it with soy and ginger while the legs still move.
Eat a small seafood bowl with ikura and uni in Donburi Yokocho.
plan-asaichi.tip: Come early morning when stalls are busy. If you ate breakfast, try the squid fishing and share one small bowl.

plan-omoide.hook: Charcoal smoke and six-seat yakitori bars under the Shinjuku train tracks.
moments: Walk into the narrow alley from Shinjuku West Exit, under red lanterns and grill smoke.
Squeeze onto a stool at a counter, your coat still on, knees touching the next person.
Order negima and tsukune skewers and watch the cook turn them over the charcoal.
Drink a cold beer or a highball while trains rumble past on the tracks next to you.
Move to a second bar for one more round of skewers.
plan-omoide.tip: Look at the menu and seat charge on the door before you go in. Bars with English menus hang them outside.

plan-daikoku.hook: The world's most famous JDM car meet, inside a giant spiral of highway ramps.
moments: Drive the Shuto Expressway at night behind the guide car, the city lights passing on both sides.
Spiral down the big loop ramp into the lot and see rows of tuned cars under orange lights.
Walk past GT-Rs, Supras, RX-7s and wild bosozoku builds, and talk to owners with your phone translator.
Warm your hands with a hot can of coffee from the vending machines.
Drive back across the lit Yokohama Bay Bridge or Rainbow Bridge.
plan-daikoku.tip: Ask the owner before you photograph a car with its owner in it. Most owners are happy to open the hood if you ask.

plan-shibuya-sky.hook: An open roof 230 m above the Scramble, with Mt Fuji at sunset.
moments: Ride the dark, light-show elevator up to the 45th floor.
Step onto the open roof and feel the cold wind at the glass edge.
Look west for Mt Fuji as the sun sets behind it, about 16:55.
Lean over the corner glass and watch the Scramble crossing fill and empty far below.
Stay until dark and watch Tokyo Tower and Skytree light up.
plan-shibuya-sky.tip: Bags, hats and loose items must go in lockers before the roof. Wear a warm jacket with zip pockets.

plan-naritasan.hook: A 1,000-year-old temple with fire rituals, 10 minutes from Narita Airport.
moments: Walk up Omotesando's winding street past old wooden shops and the smell of grilled eel.
Watch the cooks at Kawatoyo cut live eels by the front window, then eat a hot unaju.
Climb the stone steps to the Great Main Hall and sit in for a goma fire ritual with big drums.
Look up at the red and green three-storey pagoda, carved with dragons.
Walk the quiet Naritasan Park behind the temple, past ponds and a waterfall.
plan-naritasan.tip: Goma rituals run about every hour in the Main Hall. Anyone can sit in for free; be there 10 minutes early.

plan-gbc-miharashi.hook: The river steps where Nina sings for Momoka in Girls Band Cry episode 2.
moments: Walk 1 km from Kawasaki West Exit to the wide concrete steps above the Tama River.
Sit on the central stairs, where Nina sings for Momoka before Momoka moves away in ep 2.
Sit bottom right of the central stairs, Nina's guitar practice spot in ep 8.
Move to bottom left, where Tomo sees Nina practise hard in ep 9, drinking-yogurt bottle next to her.
Look across the water to Tokyo while the sun sets.
plan-gbc-miharashi.tip: Bring a small bottle of drinking yogurt for the ep 9 photo. Stamp the stamp book here.

plan-gbc-minamikawara.hook: The footbridge from the opening, where Momoka runs after Nina in episode 1.
moments: Walk into the quiet streets near Nina's apartment, past small shops and houses.
Find the Nakayoshi-maru play structure in Minamikawara Park, where Momoka gives Nina her phone in ep 1.
Climb Miyakocho Footbridge, where Momoka catches up with Nina and her lost phone in ep 1.
Stand on the east side of the bridge, face toward Shitte, and match the opening shot.
Stamp the two stamp tour points.
plan-gbc-minamikawara.tip: Go in the morning when traffic is light. Step aside for residents on the bridge stairs.

plan-gbc-muza.hook: Nina's episode 1 run, a free public piano, and anime goods upstairs.
moments: Walk the 2F deck from the station to the north escalator, Nina's route searching for Momoka in ep 1.
Play the upright piano on 1F, the piano Tomo plays in a TOGENASHI TOGEARI music video.
Look at the grand piano on 2F. It is for display only.
Shop for Girls Band Cry goods at Animate Kawasaki, then get your stamp.
plan-gbc-muza.tip: The piano is free from 10:00 to 20:00. Play one short song and let the next person have a turn.

plan-gbc-lazona.hook: The mall stage where the band plays 声なき魚 in episode 3.
moments: Walk into Rufa Square, the round open-air plaza of Lazona, west of Kawasaki Station.
Stand at the Grand Stage, where Nina, Momoka and Subaru play 声なき魚 in ep 3.
Look down on the stage from the 4F and 5F walkways, the anime's angle.
Buy Girls Band Cry goods at HMV on 4F.
Eat a warm lunch in the mall before the long walk to the river.
plan-gbc-lazona.tip: The stage area is no-photo. Keep the scene in your memory, and take photos at the other spots.

plan-gbc-east-plaza.hook: Where Nina first hears Momoka play, and where the story ends.
moments: Stand in the open plaza of the East Exit, where Momoka plays a street live in ep 1.
Find Nina's view: the plaza with the station roof and the elevated deck behind.
Find the meeting place where Nina meets Hina again in ep 13.
Buy the official stamp book for ¥500 and start the stamp tour.
Come back at night to hear real street musicians.
plan-gbc-east-plaza.tip: Take the anime-angle photos in the morning. In the evening the plaza is full of people and musicians.

plan-gbc-marufuku.hook: Coffee and a thick hotcake at the table where the band plans everything.
moments: Go down to B1F of Azalea and find the stamp beside the shop door.
Ask for the second window table from the back, where Nina sits in ep 1.
Or take the 4-person table on the left, where Rupa has her plan in ep 6.
Eat a thick, hot hotcake with butter and syrup and drink a dark Marufuku coffee.
Walk to the Girls Band Cry stamp gallery in Azalea after.
plan-gbc-marufuku.tip: Go at opening or mid-afternoon to get the anime tables. Ask staff before you take photos inside.

plan-gbc-citta.hook: The live house of the band's last show in episode 13.
moments: Walk into La Cittadella, a small Italian-style street of plazas and colored walls.
Stand at the CLUB CITTA' front entrance, the final-live venue of ep 13.
Walk the alleys the band walks on its venue visit in ep 5.
Come back after dark when the street is lit.
Look for Girls Band Cry goods at Tower Records and Village Vanguard nearby.
plan-gbc-citta.tip: Check clubcitta.co.jp before you go. On show nights there is a queue at the door, so take photos early.

plan-suga.hook: The red-railed stairs of the Your Name poster and final scene.
moments: Walk 7 minutes from Yotsuya-Sanchome through quiet back streets.
Stand at the bottom of the stairs and look up: the red railing and shrine gate match the final scene.
Take the photo where Taki and Mitsuha pass each other, then turn around.
Climb to Suga Shrine and look at the Your Name ema drawings left by fans.
plan-suga.tip: Go before 09:00. Winter morning light is soft and there is no line for the same photo.

plan-shimokita.hook: Walk Kessoku Band's home streets of live houses and used-clothing shops.
moments: Step out of Shimokitazawa Station, seen in ep 4 on the day of the band photo shoot.
Browse Village Vanguard, the goods store Bocchi passes in ep 1.
Dig through used jackets and vinyl records in the small shops on the narrow streets.
Walk the Senrogai open space above the old train line, where Bocchi sits sad in ep 5.
Eat a hot curry, Shimokitazawa's famous food, to warm up.
plan-shimokita.tip: Shops open at 11:00 to 12:00. See the anime spots first while the streets are empty.

plan-shelter.hook: The real stairs down to STARRY, Bocchi's live house.
moments: Find SHELTER's narrow door and sign on the street.
Look down the stairs into the basement, as Bocchi does with Nijika in ep 1.
Take one quiet photo of the stairs from the street.
Check the show list on the door. If a band plays that night, you can buy a ticket.
plan-shelter.tip: Come on a weekday before 14:00. SHELTER asks fans not to take photos on weekend or show evenings.

plan-nakano.hook: Four floors of used figures and manga, quieter and cheaper than Akihabara.
moments: Walk the covered Sun Mall arcade from Nakano Station into the old 1960s building.
Go up to floors 2 to 4 and walk through Mandarake's many small shops.
Look at glass cases of old figures, vintage toys and rare cards.
Search the used-manga shelves for an anime artbook you like.
Eat the tall 8-layer soft-serve at Daily Chico on B1F.
plan-nakano.tip: Most shops open about 12:00. Check each glass case price tag: many rare items cost less than in Akihabara.

plan-zest.hook: The live house from Oshi no Ko episode 1, where Ai performs.
moments: Walk the Akihabara back streets to the small venue.
Stand across the street and look at the front: it matches BEAST, Ai's live venue in ep 1.
Picture baby Aqua and Ruby in the crowd, waving glow sticks for Ai.
Walk on to atre Akihabara, another ep 1 location next to the station.
plan-zest.tip: Photograph only the outside, from across the street. Do not take photos when fans queue for a show.

plan-radio-kaikan.hook: Ten floors of figures and cards in the building from Steins;Gate episode 1.
moments: Stand across the street at the Electric Town Exit and look up at the building.
Remember Steins;Gate ep 1: Okabe goes to a time-machine talk here, and a satellite crashes on the roof.
Take the elevator to the top floor, then walk down floor by floor.
Look at glass cases of figures, model kits and trading cards on every floor.
Walk the Electric Town main street past arcades and neon signs.
plan-radio-kaikan.tip: The building in the anime was replaced by a new one in 2014. Start at the top floor to avoid walking back up.

plan-kinshi.hook: The park where Chisato and Takina talk in Lycoris Recoil episode 1.
moments: Find the benches in the middle of Kinshi Park, where Chisato and Takina talk about their cafe job in ep 1.
Stand with the play equipment on both sides and the tall buildings behind, like the anime frame.
Look up at Tokyo Skytree, lit up after 17:00, above the park.
Find the Chisato and Takina manhole cover near Olinas mall, 3 minutes from the station.
plan-kinshi.tip: The manhole was set in March 2025. Photograph it from above in daylight; at night the shadows hide the art.
